description: City partners with Quint to employ at-risk individuals.
Workers clean public spaces, remove graffiti, and pick up needles.
Project aims to reduce gang involvement and recidivism.

chips.text: Getting former gang members employed is an innovation compared to other Canadian projects.
Saskatoon is unique in Canada for addressing gangs through employment.
Public members express gratitude to workers for improving community safety.
Program supports individuals with significant criminal records and complex employment barriers.
Over 15 tons of waste and 3,308 needles removed from public spaces.

segments.title: City Staff Introduces Sweep Project
description: City staff introduced the Saskatoon Well-being Employment Enterprise Project.
The project originated from research on social enterprises with Quint.
It is funded by a federal grant to address guns and gangs.
Sweep employs at-risk individuals and partners with city departments.

chips.text: Federal Building Safer Communities grant funds the project
Employs individuals at risk of gang affiliation or formerly incarcerated
City taking a unique approach to gang reduction through employment

segments.title: Quint Details Sweep's Community Impact
description: Quint highlighted the city's leadership in using the federal fund.
Sweep employs individuals often excluded from the labor market.
The program maintains public spaces and improves community safety.
Work includes cleaning transit shelters and removing waste.

chips.text: Public spaces, including art, transit shelters, parks, and alleys
Former gang members remove gang graffiti and former drug dealers pick up needles
Procurement dollars from various city departments used for social enterprise

segments.title: Employment Transition and Program Stability
description: Councillor Timone asked about individuals transitioning to mainstream employment.
Quint focuses on long-term stabilization due to complex barriers.
The program aims to build work skills before external transitions.
Successful transitions have occurred, but not all original employees remain.

chips.text: Supports individuals facing complex barriers to mainstream employment
Extended employment period helps individuals navigate personal and family stresses

segments.title: Client Recruitment and Program Capacity
description: Quint recruits clients through transition homes and reintegration units.
The program has budget limitations and a long waiting list.
Wraparound supports include stable housing and family reunification.
Nearly 25 individuals have participated in the program.

chips.text: Provides wraparound support for housing, family, and justice system navigation
Program faces budget limitations despite high demand for services

segments.title: Addressing Specific Client Barriers
description: Councillor Parker requested specific examples of client barriers.
Quint described challenges with basic life skills and self-esteem.
Support includes system navigation and advocacy for criminal records.
An anecdote highlighted a client's dedication despite physical injury.

chips.text: Supports individuals with significant criminal records in system navigation
Client had a bullet removed and wanted to return to work immediately

segments.title: Social Enterprise as a Different Approach
description: Mayor Block asked about the program's unique approach.
Quint views marginalized communities as valuable resources, not burdens.
Social enterprise offers a different employment option for individuals.
The city acts as a leader in promoting this business model.

chips.text: City promotes social enterprise as a model for community development
Social enterprise bottom line includes social and cultural aspects, not just profit

segments.title: Program Funding and Future Procurement
description: The program is federally funded through the Building Safer Communities Fund.
Its innovative approach involves employing former gang members.
A Special Projects Manager coordinates work opportunities with city departments.
The city currently lacks procurement targets for social enterprises.

chips.text: Funding for Special Projects Manager until March 31, 2026
City currently lacks procurement targets for social enterprises
Employing marginalized people reduces illegal economies and policing costs
